abstract: Abstract Purpose: Anaesthesia is commonly required to immobilise mice in preclinical ophthalmic studies but also alters systemic physiology. We investigate the effects of three anaesthetics on optoretinography (ORG) measurements obtained by functional optical coherence tomography (OCT). Methods: A total of 14 adult C57BL/6J mice (5 female and 9 male) were grouped in three cohorts. Each cohort was alternatingly exposed to isoflurane (ISO), ketamine-xylazine (KX) and a mixture of medetomidine, midazolam, fentanyl and ketamine (MMFK). ORG measurements were recorded by functional OCT 15 and 30 minutes after induction using a brief 502 nm light stimulus. The time to peak contraction, contraction amplitude and the elongation slope were extracted from ORG traces. Furthermore, a spectral analysis was performed on the respiratory rate acquired from the OCT data between both sexes. All parameters were statistically analysed using a linear mixed effects model with Holm-Bonferroni correction. Results: Statistically significant differences were observed for some ORG parameters. The contraction amplitude for mice was greater and slope was lower comparing when anaesthetised with ISO compared to MMFK at 15 minutes post induction. Additionally, for both sexes, statistically significant differences were observed for the respiratory rate of mice anaesthetised with ISO compared to those under MMFK and KX. Conclusions: All three anaesthetic protocols permitted ORG acquisition. However, anaesthesia-dependent effects on ORG parameters and respiratory rate should be considered when interpreting and comparing ORG data.
